claim: The Colli Euganei is one of Italy's few volcanic wine districts and the identity of the appellation is inseparable from Bordeaux varieties — Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Carménère — that have thrived for more than two centuries.
quote: The identity of the Colli Euganei is inseparable from its volcanic origins and the Bordeaux grape varieties—Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, and Carménère—that have thrived here for more than two centuries.

claim: The Euganean Hills rise 300–600m from the Padovan-Venetian plain and the vines are rooted in basaltic, mineral-rich soils that lend the wines depth and a distinctive savoury character.
quote: The vines are rooted in basaltic, mineral-rich soils, which lend the wines depth, structure, and a distinctive savory character.

claim: Colli Euganei Fior d'Arancio DOCG is Italy's only DOCG dedicated exclusively to aromatic Moscato Giallo, produced in still, sparkling and passito styles after promotion from DOC to DOCG in 2011.
quote: These sweet wines were sold under the Colli Euganei DOC title for a long time, but in 2011 their stand-out style and consistently high quality were officially recognised, and they were granted promotion to full, independent DOCG status.

claim: Vignalta in Arquà Petrarca, the largest producer of Colli Euganei DOC and Fior d'Arancio DOCG, is open Monday to Sunday 10:00–18:00 and offers a private tasting + cellar tour for €25 with 24-hour booking confirmation by email.
quote: Via Scalette 23, Arquà Petrarca, 35032, Italy ... Monday to Sunday from 10 am to 6 pm ... wineshop@vignalta.it

claim: Cantina Maeli in Baone runs three bookable tasting experiences focused on Moscato Giallo / Fior d'Arancio, with the standard tasting around €31.50–€35, rated 4.9 stars on Google.
quote: Welcome to Maeli ... Maeli Top Wine Tasting ... La via del Moscato giallo

claim: Ca' Lustra Zanovello in Faedo (Cinto Euganeo) offers a 'Classic Tasting' (4 wines plus cheese and bread) and a 'Deluxe Tasting' (guided vineyard + cellar tour with 6 wines), bookable daily in English for individuals or small groups.
quote: The Deluxe Tasting is a complete and exclusive experience that includes a guided tour through the vineyards and cellar, followed by tasting 6 wines

claim: Conte Emo Capodilista – La Montecchia in Selvazzano Dentro borders the Euganei park and is one of the closest serious estates to Rubano, owned by the family since the 15th century with 45 hectares of vines around the frescoed Villa Emo Capodilista.
quote: Via Montecchia 16 - 35030 Selvazzano Dentro (PD) ... La Montecchia welcomes those who want to organize tastings, holidays in the medieval town, in the castle or, exceptionally, in Villa Emo Capodilista, overlooking the vineyards.

claim: Borin Vini & Vigne sits in the Regional Park of the Colli Euganei between Monselice and Arquà Petrarca, with 26 of its 38 hectares planted to vines and 18 wines produced across four collections including a Fior d'Arancio DOCG.
quote: The Borin estate lies in the municipal areas of Monselice and Arquà Petrarca, in the Regional Nature Park of the Colli Euganei. Of the 38 hectares of land owned by the family, around 26 hectares are vineyards.

claim: Salvan – Vigne del Pigozzo conducts tastings personally led by the winemaker family (Giorgio, Rosanna, or Francesca), pouring at least 7 wines including indigenous Friularo and Turchetta.
quote: Through the tasting of at least 7 wines, visitors can discover the rich history of an area with a long winemaking tradition: going back to the time of the Venetians, with indigenous wines such as Friularo and Turchetta.

claim: Caffè Pedrocchi at Via VIII Febbraio 15 has operated for almost 200 years and serves its trademark coffee — espresso with mint cream and cocoa — which the house instructs you to drink without sugar or stirring.
quote: You shouldn't add any sugar nor stir it… Come and find out why!

claim: Pedrocchi opened in 1831 from Jappelli's neoclassical design and was nicknamed the 'café without doors' because it stayed open day and night until 1916; the Piano Nobile upstairs holds the Museum of the Risorgimento, ticket €4.
quote: From its inauguration in 1831 until 1916, it was always open, day and night, earning it the reputation of the "café without doors".

claim: Sotto il Salone, the covered market beneath the Palazzo della Ragione, has functioned continuously for nearly 800 years and houses more than fifty small shops selling cheeses, cured meats, wine and prepared food — the oldest covered shopping centre still in operation in Europe.
quote: the most ancient covered market in Europe ... more than fifty small shops offering quality food products such as cheeses, meats and cured meats from throughout Italy

claim: The open-air Piazza delle Erbe produce market runs Monday–Friday 07:00–13:30 and Saturday 07:30–20:00 with ~70 stalls of fruit, vegetables, legumes, cereals, flowers and seeds; closed Sunday.
quote: Monday-Friday: 7 am – 1:30 pm ... Saturday: 7:30 am – 8 pm ... approximately 70 stalls

claim: Padovan cuisine centres on gallina padovana (a dark-meat, crested heritage hen breed), bigoli (thick fresh spaghetti pushed through a bigolaro press), risi e bisi (spring rice and peas with pancetta), and bigoli with oca in onto (preserved goose).
quote: Bigoli are thick spaghetti prepared with flour, eggs, water and salt and then passed through a press called a bigolaro

claim: The Gallina Padovana breed is distinguished by a large head crest and beard with darker, more delicate meat than standard chicken, and is the basis of a classic local braise with tomato, onion, white wine and herbs.
quote: The breed is distinguished by the large crest that adorns the head and the beard under the beak, as well as for the meat which is darker than traditional chicken but more delicate and tasty.

claim: Aperol was created in 1919 by brothers Luigi and Silvio Barbieri and debuted at the Padova World Fair that year; the modern Prosecco-based spritz emerged in the 1970s and Veneto now consumes nearly 300,000 spritzes a day.
quote: Aperol came onto the scene in 1919, created by brothers Luigi and Silvio Barbieri in Padova. They debuted Aperol at the 1919 Padova World Fair.

claim: Padova's piazzas, arcades and historic centre are the canonical setting to drink spritz, which the city tourism board calls 'an undeniable part of Padova's life and atmosphere' and an official IBA cocktail since 2011.
quote: an undeniable part of Padova's life and atmosphere

claim: Veneto Euganei e Berici DOP olive oil is produced in 15 municipalities around the Euganean Hills Regional Park from Leccino and Rasara (minimum 50%) blended with Frantoio, Maurino and other local varieties.
quote: The oil is obtained from the Leccino and Rasara varieties (at least 50%) and the Frantoio, Maurino, Pendolino, Marzemino, Riondella, Trep or Drop or Matosso varieties

claim: Colli Euganei DOP olive oil shows an intense golden-green colour with a fruity aroma and low acidity, a product of the mild Euganean microclimate combined with volcanic soils — olive cultivation in the hills dates to the 15th-century Venetian Republic.
quote: Thanks to the combination of mild climate and volcanic soil, the extra virgin oil of Colli Euganei is one of the agricultural and food excellences of Veneto, appreciated for its harmonious taste and low acidity.

claim: Asparago Bianco di Bassano DOP — milk-white, fibreless, sweet-bitter — is harvested mid-March to mid-June, so a late-May visit hits peak season; classic Veneto preparations are risotto agli asparagi and asparagi con le uova.
quote: the production period goes from mid-March to mid-June
